Ivy: Flagging a confusing UI case: per-model card shows cache savings > token cost for some low-volume routes (tenant T). Example: cost $0.09, cache savings $0.22. Screenshot in thread.
Marc: That usually points to sampling or amortization mismatch. Which panel was this in?
Ivy: exploration 24h. I pulled the rollup row: token_cost_24h=0.09, cache_credit_24h=0.22, sample_coverage=7%.
Sofia: 7% coverage explains large variance. UX-wise we should avoid alarming numbers. Proposal: console derives "Estimated cache savings" = min(cache_credit_24h, token_cost_24h) when coverage <25% and shows a confidence pill (low/med/high).
Ken: Backend should still emit canonical fields: token_cost_24h, cache_credit_24h, cache_credit_7d_amortized, sample_count, rollup_version. Console can compute the clamped view.
Marc: I'll add a small SQL change to rollup job to emit both windows and sample_count (RED-ENG-8001). Ken: can you own console flag for clamped display (RED-ENG-8002)?
Ken: yes. UX microcopy draft: "Estimated cache savings (clamped to observed token cost). Based on sampled telemetry; see confidence for coverage"
Ivy: also request an alert rule: if cache_credit_24h > token_cost_24h * 2 and sample_coverage < 30% -> create QA ticket (non-billing) so we can investigate sampling issues.
ops-bot: Created issues RED-ENG-8001, RED-ENG-8002, RED-ENG-8003.
Sofia: rollout plan: land rollup fields then enable console flag behind FF, canary to 10 tenants for 48h, then expand.
Ivy: thanks all. I'll attach tenant sample rows to RED-ENG-8001.
